tasks.title: HANGS Construction Services · FY2026 Cash Audit
tasks.description: Audit HANGS Construction Services LLC’s cash at June 30, 2026 from 10 Excel and PDF files: the trial balance, the cash ledger, the statements and the company’s two bank reconciliations, the confirmation the audit team sent, the bank’s confirmation and supplementary reply, the June statements, the July cutoff statement and the bank’s incoming payments report, all sent to the audit team directly. Tie cash across the books, agree the confirmation, recompute the reconciliations, trace every outstanding item, test cut-off and restrictions and set what was found against materiality. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.

light.reason: Waiting for review: draft package ready, open items remain

propertyEvents.result: Propose materiality from revenue, as the audit plan sets it
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-2; balance sheet, income statement and the notes

propertyEvents.result: Revenue $68,989,500.00 x 0.5% = $344,947.50, rounded down to $340,000.00, the same as the year-end audit. Performance materiality $255,000.00; clearly trivial $17,000.00. Cash is $5,534,665.71, 25.6% of total assets, so a misstatement of cash matters mostly through what it hides. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.

propertyEvents.explanation: Materiality is the size of mistake that would change what a reader of the statements decides. Performance materiality is set lower so small errors cannot add up unnoticed. Anything under the clearly trivial amount is listed but not added up.

propertyEvents.result: The bank debited the payroll account $4,065.00 in FY2026: 12 monthly charges of $315.00 or $410.00, July 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026. None of the 664 cash lines in the books is a bank charge, so none was recorded: payroll cash is overstated and expenses understated by $4,065.00. The reconciliation carried them as a reconciling item instead of booking them.

propertyEvents.result: Test the wires, transfers and receipts either side of June 30
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; the June 2026 statements of both accounts, every line and the closing balances

propertyEvents.result: $90,000.00 left by wire on June 30, 2026 for the quarter’s dividend and is in the books that day; the 4 quarterly wires make the $360,000.00 of dividends in the trial balance. The 2 transfers to the payroll account on June 25, $364,679.10, are in both accounts on the same day, and there is none July 1 to 8. The last June receipts, 4 wires of June 29 ($2,944,466.17), are on the June statement and in the June books. The first after year end, Pier Nine Commercial LLC’s check 40815 dated June 29, reached the lockbox July 1 and was credited July 2, $1,957,000.00: correctly a July receipt, and still a receivable at June 30.
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; the June 2026 statements of both accounts, every line and the closing balances

tape.label: First July Receipt, Pier Nine, July 2

propertyEvents.result: Look for cash that is held back, pledged or restricted, what the loans require, and what the statements would need to say
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; service charges, check 21561, stale checks, holds, liens, set-off and compensating balances

propertyEvents.result: The bank reports no holds, liens, pledges or compensating balance, and the loan agreement requires none: the bank’s right of set-off applies only on a default. The owners’ retainage, $1,161,125.00, is a receivable (account 1250), not cash held back. No restricted cash. But all $5,723,107.14 is at one bank, $5,473,107.14 above the FDIC’s $250,000.00 insurance, and the draft notes say nothing of it: a concentration of credit risk the CPA decides on (DISC-01).
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; service charges, check 21561, stale checks, holds, liens, set-off and compensating balances

propertyEvents.result: Wires, transfers and receipts are in the right year · no restricted cash · uninsured balances for the CPA
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

One known misstatement of income: the payroll account charges (FEE-01), $4,065.00, under the $17,000.00 clearly trivial, so it is listed but not added up; proposed: debit bank charges, credit payroll cash. Stale check 21561 (STALE-01), $21,850.80, is above clearly trivial: voiding it puts cash back and shows the payable still owed (or unclaimed property), a classification with no effect on income, 8.6% of the $255,000.00 performance materiality. Together cash rises $17,785.80. Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.

tape.label: FEE-01 Payroll Account Charges, Clearly Trivial
Net Effect on Cash if Both Recorded

events.result: The bank reports no holds, liens, pledges or compensating balance, and the loan agreement requires none: the bank’s right of set-off applies only on a default. The owners’ retainage, $1,161,125.00, is a receivable (account 1250), not cash held back. No restricted cash.
